items.title: SK하이닉스 "2029년까지 D램·HBM 물량 완판…중장기 판매 가시성 높아져"(종합)

items.title: 與 “조희대 국조 실시… 내달 5일 본회의 상정”
items.snippet: 더불어민주당이 대법관 후보자 재제청 거부 등을 사유로 조희대 대법원장에 대한 국정조사를 실시하기로 했다. 사법부 수장에 대한 입법부의 국정조사는 처음이다. 국민의힘은 “노골적인 사법부 탄압이고 명백한 삼권분립 위반”이라고 반발했다. 민주당 한병도 원내대표는 27일 의원총회에서 “대법관 재제청 거부와 공백 장기화부터 현금 격려금과 업무추진비 집행까지 조 대법원장 본인을 둘러싼 의혹도 겹겹이 쌓이고 있다”며 “제기된 의혹을 철저히 규명하고 국민적 의구심을 해소하는 것은 국회가 마땅히 해야 할 책무”라고 밝혔다. 전은수 원내대변인은 비공개 의총을 마친 뒤 기자들과 만나 “조 대법원장에 대한 국정조사를 해야 한다는 데 의견이 모아졌고, 국정조사를 실시하기로 했다”고 했다. 민주당은 다음 달 5일 국회 본회의에 국정조사 요구서를 보고하고, 다음 12일...

items.title: 애기봉 1.4㎞ 앞, 南 겨눈 北 자주포
items.snippet: 북한 병사들이 27일 경기 김포시 애기봉에서 약 1.4km 떨어진 황해북도 개풍군 일원에서 깃발을 흔들며 덕천포(M-1975 122mm 자주포) 정비 및 발사 준비 훈련을 하고 있다. 북한이 최근 전술적 타격 수단의 증강 배치를 거론한 가운데 의도적으로 자주포를 노출시키며 무력 과시를 하고 있다는 분석이 나온다.

items.title: 與도 시행 두달 남은 ‘코인과세’ 유예 의견 모아
items.snippet: 정부가 내년 1월로 예정된 가상자산 과세를 다시 유예하는 쪽에 무게를 두고 있는 가운데 여당도 27일 의원총회에서 과세를 미뤄야 한다는 쪽으로 가닥을 잡은 것으로 전해졌다. 여당은 정부와 28일 당정협의를 열고 이 같은 의견을 전달할 예정이다. 더불어민주당 김한규 원내정책수석부대표는 이날 의원총회를 마친 뒤 기자들과 만나 “가상자산 과세 유예 자체에 반대하는 분은 없고 오히려 유예가 필요하다는 개인 의견들이 나왔다”며 “분위기는 유예 쪽으로 모아지고 있는 게 아닌가 싶다”고 밝혔다. 예정대로 과세를 시행해야 한다는 의견보다는 유예론에 힘이 실렸다는 의미다. 이날 의원총회 토론에서는 디지털자산기본법을 먼저 제정한 뒤 가상자산 과세를 함께 시행해야 한다는 의견도 제시된 것으로 알려졌다. 가상자산의 법적 지위를 정하는 디지털자산기본법을 통해 발행·...

items.title: 曺 겨눈 與, 대법관 재제청 거부 경위-계엄당시 회의 조사 거론
items.snippet: 더불어민주당이 27일 의원총회에서 조희대 대법원장을 겨냥한 국정조사를 추진하기로 하면서 조 대법원장에 대한 공세를 본격화했다. 지난해 이재명 대통령의 공직선거법 사건에 대한 대법원의 파기환송 판결 이후 이어져 왔던 여권과 조 대법원장 간의 긴장관계가 대법관 후보자 재제청 거부 사태로 초유의 대법원장에 대한 국정조사로 이어진 것. 조 대법원장은 이날 퇴근길에 국정조사 추진에 대해 묻는 취재진의 질문에 답하지 않았다.● 與 “다음 달 5일 국조 계획서 본회의 보고” 민주당 전은수 원내대변인은 이날 의원총회를 마친 뒤 “조 대법원장 향후 조치와 관련해 국정조사를 해야 한다는 데 의견이 모아졌고, 실시하기로 했다”며 “국조를 해서 밝힐 것들을 밝혀야 한다는 것”이라고 했다. 당초 당내 강경파와 조국혁신당 등을 중심으로 즉시 탄핵에 나서야 한다는 의견...

items.title: 강경파는 “국조 말고 바로 탄핵해야”
items.snippet: 더불어민주당이 의원총회에서 조희대 대법원장에 대한 탄핵 추진에 앞서 국정조사를 실시하기로 결정했지만 친청(친정청래)계 등 강경파와 조국혁신당에서는 “국정조사가 아니라 바로 탄핵을 해야 한다”는 주장이 나온다. 국정조사는 이르면 연말에 끝날 것으로 예상되는 만큼 그 이후 탄핵소추안을 의결하면 조 대법원장 퇴임까지 헌법재판소 결정이 나오지 않을 수 있다는 주장이다. 27일 민주당은 다음 달 5일 열리는 본회의에서 조 대법원장 관련 국정조사요구서를 보고할 예정이라고 밝혔다. 이후 1, 2주 동안 여야 협의 등을 거쳐 국정조사계획서를 채택하겠다는 방침이다. 국정조사는 40∼50일간 진행될 것으로 예상된다. 가장 최근에 실시된 6월 6·3 지방선거 투표용지 부족 사태 국정조사의 기간은 45일이었고, 3월 윤석열 정권 정치검찰 조작기소 국정조사는 50일...

items.title: 與 ‘조희대 휴대전화 교체 내역’ 조회 논란
items.snippet: 국회 과학기술정보방송통신위원회 소속 의원들이 국정감사 기간 동안 조희대 대법원장의 휴대전화 기기 교체 내역을 확인한 사실이 드러났다. 자료를 요구한 더불어민주당 황정아 의원은 27일 “국회의 적법한 의결 자료에 대해 ‘사찰’이라는 식으로 몰고 가는 것에 대해 깊은 유감을 표한다”고 밝혔다. 국회에 따르면 과방위는 22일 황 의원실 요구로 SK텔레콤, KT, LG유플러스 등 이동통신 3사로부터 제출받은 조 대법원장의 휴대전화 기기 변경 내역 유무와 시점, 기종 등과 관련된 자료를 열람했다. 제출된 자료에는 특정 기간 동안 조 대법원장의 ‘휴대전화 기기 변경 내역이 없다’는 답변과 함께 조 대법원장의 개인 휴대전화 번호가 포함됐다. 이에 정치권에서 사생활 침해와 사찰 논란이 제기되자 황 의원은 적법한 절차에 따라 의결해 제출받은 자료라는 취지로...

items.title: 李, 중수청장 배석 논란에 “비정상의 정상화… 한달에 한번쯤 오라”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 27일 “비정상의 정상화”라며 중대범죄수사청장(중수청장) 등 수사기관장의 국무회의 참석 원칙을 고수했다. 다만 “다른 일이 있는데 억지로 올 필요는 없다”며 “그래도 한 달에 한 번쯤은 오라”고 했다. 수사기관장의 국무회의 참석이 독립성과 정치적 중립성을 훼손한다는 비판을 재차 반박하면서도 ‘조건부 참석’이라는 절충안을 택한 것으로 풀이된다.● 李 “중수청장, 한 달에 한 번쯤 오라” 이 대통령은 이날 청와대에서 주재한 국무회의에서 “비정상에 오랫동안 노출되다 보면 그 비정상이 정상인 것처럼 오인되고, 오히려 정상이 비정상으로 이해되는 경우도 많다”며 “그런 잘못된 관행이나 일종의 열외 등을 시정하는 게 개혁이고 발전”이라고 말했다. 과거 검찰총장 등 수사기관장이 정치적 중립과 수사 독립을 고려해 국무회의에 참석하지 않았던 관...

items.title: [단독]‘경기·성남-민주당-중앙대’ 출신, 李정부 임명 공공기관 임원 20% 차지
items.snippet: 이재명 정부 출범 후 임명된 공공기관 임원 5명 중 1명은 ‘경기·성남 라인’ 등 이 대통령과 관계가 있는 인물로 채워졌다는 주장이 나왔다. 일부 인사들은 국정감사 과정에서 불공정 채용 의혹까지 불거지면서 야권은 “낙하산 인사”라고 비판하고 나섰다. 27일 국민의힘 김승수 의원실이 공공기관 경영정보 공개시스템 ‘알리오’에 게재된 공기업·준정부기관·기타공공기관 342곳의 임원 현황 공시를 분석한 결과 이재명 정부 출범 이후 새로 선임된 상임 임원은 364명이었다. 김 의원실은 이 중 20%인 74명이 인맥·학맥 등으로 이 대통령 및 현 정권과 연결고리가 있는 것으로 봤다. 23명은 이 대통령이 성남시장, 경기도지사일 때 연이 있는 경기·성남 라인으로 분류됐고, 더불어민주당 소속으로 의원직이나 당직 등을 지낸 인물은 31명이었다. 17명은 민주당...

items.title: 견제 주고받는 ‘장-이-한’, 吳에 구애 동상이몽
items.snippet: 오세훈 서울시장이 여론조사비 대납 의혹 항소심에서 무죄를 선고받은 가운데 국민의힘 장동혁 대표, 개혁신당 이준석 의원, 무소속 한동훈 의원이 오 시장과 동상이몽의 ‘사각관계’를 형성했다는 분석이 나온다. 장 대표와 이 의원, 한 의원이 서로 각을 세우면서도 오 시장을 향해선 구애에 나서고 있는 것. 6·3 지방선거 당시 오 시장과 갈등을 거듭했던 장 대표는 26일 국립서울현충원에서 열린 박정희 전 대통령 추모식에서 오 시장과 만나 웃으며 악수했다. 이날 오 시장이 “특검이 상고를 포기해야 한다는 목소리를 내주셔서 고맙다”고 하자, 장 대표는 “대표로서 당연히 할 일”이라고 답했다.이 의원은 오 시장이 항소심 선고 당시 서울고법을 찾은 국민의힘 의원 8명을 26일 초청한 만찬에 참석했다. 이 의원은 만찬에서 “오뚝이처럼, 세파를 이겨내니, 훈풍...

items.title: [단독]北, 남포 등서 잠수정으로 대남 해상 침투훈련
items.snippet: 북한이 남포 등 일부 지역에서 잠수함정과 공작모선 등 침투 훈련을 이어온 정황을 정보당국이 포착한 것으로 알려졌다. 북한이 비무장지대(DMZ) 지뢰 폭발 사건 이후 접경지역 일대 국지 도발 위협 수위를 높이는 가운데 대남 공작 활동을 강화하려는 움직임을 보이고 있는 것으로 풀이된다. 27일 정부 고위 소식통은 “정보당국이 북한이 하계훈련을 계기로 이런 훈련을 지속해 온 동향을 주시하고 있는 것으로 안다”고 전했다. 공작모선은 공작원이나 소형 잠수정, 침투 장비 등을 싣고 이동하면서 목표 해역에서 이들을 투입하거나 회수하는 모선(母船) 역할을 하는 선박이다.정보당국은 이 같은 북한의 동향이 최근 북한 정찰총국의 정찰정보총국 확대 개편 움직임과 맞물려 진행되고 있는 것으로 분석하고 있다. 앞서 7월 북한 노동당 중앙군사위원회 확대회의에서 김정은...

items.title: “미군 믿을수 있냐”는 강신철에… 野 “동맹 흔드는 망언, 경질을”

items.title: ‘서울 마지막 판자촌’ 강남 구룡마을 화재… 강풍까지 불어 진압 난항
items.snippet: 27일 오후 서울 강남구 구룡마을에서 큰불이 나 화염과 검은 연기가 치솟고 있다. 불길이 판잣집을 타고 번지면서 주민 39명이 긴급 대피했다. 강남 일대에는 매캐한 연기가 퍼졌다. 소방 당국은 “오후 11시 현재 인명 피해는 없다”며 “강풍이 불고 용수가 부족해 진압에 시간이 걸리고 있다”고 밝혔다. 구룡마을은 서울의 마지막 판자촌으로 불린다. 2023년 1월과 올 1월에도 큰불이 났다. 이재명 대통령은 “가용한 자원을 총동원해 인명 구조와 안전 확보에 만전을 기하라”고 지시했다. 오세훈 서울시장은 국회의원 만찬 등 일정을 취소하고 현장을 찾아 점검했다.

items.snippet: 기후에너지환경부는 사라질 위기에 처한 ‘멸종 위기 야생생물’을 매달 한 종류씩 자세히 알리고 있어요. 이달의 멸종 위기 야생생물은 두드럭조개랍니다. 조개 하면 대합·홍합·바지락·꼬막처럼 맛있는 바다 조개가 먼저 떠오르는데요. 민물조개인 두드럭조개는 강의 오염을 막아주는 수질 청정기 역할을 해 온 고마운 친구랍니다. 두드럭조개라는 재미있는 이름은 껍데기 표면이 마치 두드러기가 난 것처럼 오톨도톨한 작은 돌기들로 덮여 있다는 데서 유래했어요. 다 자라면 껍데기 길이가 9㎝에 달해 민물조개치고는 아주 큰 편이죠. 기다란 만큼 두께도 두툼한 데다 안쪽에는 아름다운 광택이 돌아서 단추 재료로 인기가 많아 일본에 수출까지 했을 정도랍니다.

items.snippet: ‘오늘’을 기준으로 다음 날을 ‘내일’, 그다음 날은 ‘모레’라고 합니다. 그렇다면 ‘모레’의 다음 날은 무엇일까요? 정답은 ‘글피’입니다. 오늘을 기준으로 하루, 이틀, 사흘, 나흘 뒤는 차례대로 ‘내일’, ‘모레’, ‘글피’, ‘그글피’라고 부릅니다. 예를 들어 오늘이 월요일이라면 내일은 화요일, 모레는 수요일, 글피는 목요일, 그글피는 금요일이지요.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [알립니다] 중등 NIE 11·12월 수강생 모집

items.title: ZnO/Ni interface-activated enhancement of spintronic terahertz emission from Ni/Pt bilayers
items.abstract: Spintronic terahertz (THz) emitters based on ferromagnet/heavy-metal bilayers provide an efficient route for generating broadband THz radiation through ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion. However, Ni/Pt bilayers usually exhibit relatively weak THz emission, limiting their use as efficient spintronic emitters. Here, we report an interface-assisted enhancement of THz emission in ZnO/Ni/Pt heterostructures. By placing ZnO underneath Ni while preserving the direct Ni/Pt contact, the THz amplitude is increased by up to approximately 2.8 times compared with the Ni/Pt reference. The enhanced emission reverses polarity with the magnetic field and follows the expected angular dependence of ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion. ZnO-, Ni-, and Pt-thickness-dependent measurements show that the emission remains governed by the Ni/Pt conversion process but is strongly affected by the ZnO/Ni bottom int...

items.title: Machine Learning Hamiltonians with Polarizations for Heterogeneous Systems
items.abstract: Machine learning Hamiltonians use local atomic structures to determine local Hamiltonian matrix elements without carrying out self-consistent calculations. They have been used to study large systems and to carry out high-throughput screening for their electronic and optical properties. The prediction of the Hamiltonian is essentially the prediction of the electron electrostatic potential energy; however, for heterogeneous systems, this potential energy is often determined by faraway features, such as interface or surface dipoles, or even an applied voltage in a nanodevice. Thus, it cannot be determined by local atomic structures alone. In this sense, one needs to solve the electron electrostatic potential energy self-consistently using intrinsic atomic dipoles, the applied external potential energy, and polarizabilities. items.title: Demonstration of high output power (3.75 W/mm) with 31.8% PAE in Ga-Polar AlGaN/GaN HEMTs on sapphire at 94 GHz
items.abstract: In this work, a recessed-gate Ga-polar AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) on sapphire incorporating an AlGaN back-barrier for W-band operation is demonstrated. The device achieves a subthreshold slope of ~130 mV/dec, a peak transconductance of 0.75 S/mm, and an fmax exceeding 240 GHz. Continuous-wave load-pull measurements at 94 GHz show an output power of 3.75 W/mm with a power-added efficiency of 31.8%. This performance significantly exceeds the best previously reported Ga-polar devices on sapphire and approaches that of state-of-the-art Ga-polar devices on SiC, which provides a promising pathway toward high-performance W-band devices.

items.title: Coherent Optical Control of a Single Donor Electron Spin
items.abstract: Coherent spin-photon interfaces are essential for scalable quantum networks, but their realization requires optically bright transitions, long-lived spin coherence, and complete coherent control. Donor-bound electron spins in II-VI semiconductors offer an attractive platform for optically active spin qubits because they combine strong donor-bound exciton transitions in a direct-bandgap material with a potentially nuclear-spin-free environment. However, coherent control of an individual optically active donor spin has remained elusive. Here we demonstrate optical initialization, coherent control, and readout of a single donor-bound electron spin in ZnSe. Using spin-selective donor-bound exciton optical transitions, we initialize the electron spin and directly resolve its spin-relaxation dynamics. items.abstract: Compact optical systems with continuously tunable focal lengths are highly desirable for machine vision, biomedical imaging, and miniaturized cameras. Rotational Moiré lenses offer a planar approach to focal-length tuning, but metasurface-based implementations typically require complex nanofabrication processes that complicate large-area production. Here, we present a cyclic, mask-free fabrication strategy that combines layer-by-layer self-assembly of two-dimensional graphene oxide (GO) and poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (PDDA) with femtosecond laser nanoprinting. Repeated GO-PDDA assembly and spatially selective ablation enable atomic-scale thickness control and the construction of precise multilevel phase profiles, reducing phase-quantization errors and improving focusing efficiency. items.title: Generation of quantum light with tunable Wigner negativity with a semiconductor quantum dot
items.abstract: Wigner-negative states of light are key resources for quantum advantage in continuous-variable optical quantum computing. They can be produced probabilistically via frequency conversion and photon detection, or deterministically by exploiting the single-photon nonlinearity of a quantum emitter. Here, we generate such Wigner-negative states of light with a tunable negativity using a single semiconductor quantum dot in a cavity. Optical coherent control of the quantum-dot transition allows to generate a quantum superposition of zero and one photon. The generated quantum states are characterized point-by-point in the phase space through homodyne measurement. The emergence of Wigner-function negativity is observed as the excitation power is increased. items.title: “국비 확보 10조원 시대 열어 대구 경제 대전환”
items.snippet: 추경호 대구시장은 전통 경제 관료 출신으로 시작해 나라 살림을 책임지는 경제부총리까지 지냈다. 여기에 대구 달성군 3선 국회의원에, 여당 원내대표로 정치인으로 10년 경험을 쌓았다. 중앙 행정에 정치 인맥까지 갖췄다는 평가를 받는 이유다. 40여 년간 쌓은 행정·정치 노하우는 국비 확보로 확인됐다. 대구시의 내년도 국비 확보액은 역대 최대다. 추 시장은 “국정감사가 마무리되면 이달 말부터 본격적인 국회 예산 심의가 시작된다”며 “정부안에 미반영된 사업을 하나하나 다시 점검하고, 지역 국회의원들과 원팀으로 대응해 대구시 최초로 국비 10조원 시대를 열어 보이겠다”고 자신감을 보였다.

Multimode continuous-variable quantum key distribution with CMOS-compatible photonic-electronic integration
items.abstract: Multiplexing and photonic-electronic integration offer a route to scalable and high-throughput quantum key distribution (QKD) networks through parallel transmission and compact hardware suited to volume manufacturing. Realizing this route requires multichannel transmitters and receivers, and a security analysis accounting for mode coupling. Here we present a CMOS-compatible photonic-electronic multimode continuous-variable QKD architecture, using polarization multiplexing as a two-mode example. Silicon-photonic transmitter and receiver chips prepare and detect two polarization modes in parallel. The receiver is co-integrated with a dual-channel 28-nm CMOS transimpedance amplifier, providing shot-noise clearances exceeding 20 dB in both channels. items.title: Optical Thermometry in Monolayer WS2: Raman and Photoluminescence Spectroscopy from 5 K to 1273 K
items.abstract: Reliable temperature measurement is essential for characterizing and engineering two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor devices, yet optical thermometry of 2D materials has so far been demonstrated only over narrow temperature windows spanning a few hundred kelvin. Here, we establish a comprehensive optical thermometry framework for monolayer WS2 from 5~K to 1273~K. We show that: (i) the out-of-plane A1g Raman mode shifts linearly with temperature above 100~K, with a slope of -0.0138 cm^{-1}/K in non-encapsulated WS2 (fitted over 298-1223~K) and a measurably smaller slope of -0.0121 cm^{-1}/K in an hBN-encapsulated sample (fitted over 100-1273~K); (ii) photoluminescence spectra measured over the same 5--1273~K range provide an independent optical indicator of the temperature: the neutral-exciton emission redshifts continuously with temperature and is well described by the semi-empirical Päss...

items.title: A van der Waals Floating-Gate Platform for Broadband Optoelectronic Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Artificial synapses that integrate nonvolatile memory with broadband optoelectronic learning are essential for next-generation neuromorphic computing. However, their realization remains challenging because conventional floating-gate memories exhibit limited optical functionality and poor scalability. Here, we report a van der Waals ReS2/hBN/InSe floating-gate synaptic transistor that combines efficient charge storage with broadband optoelectronic learning in a single device architecture. The heterostructure incorporates InSe as a floating-gate layer for stable charge storage, hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) as a tunneling dielectric, and ReS2 as a photoresponsive channel, enabling carrier tunneling under electrical and optical stimulation. items.title: Photoinduced charging and spatially selective photochemistry on ferroelectric surfaces
items.abstract: Ferroelectric surfaces exhibit polarization-dependent photoreactivity and provide a route to program chemical patterns through local electrical control of polarization. Observations accumulated over several decades show reaction products in domain interiors, at domain boundaries, and in other selected regions, indicating that the mechanisms extend beyond a single polarization-induced band-bending picture. Here we analyze light-induced charging and interfacial reactions on uniformly polarized ferroelectrics and domain patterns, for dry surfaces and surfaces in contact with an electrochemically active solution. items.title: ChroNoC: A Tableless TDM Circuit-Switched NoC With Delay-Aware Deployment for Time-Sensitive Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Time-sensitive neuromorphic architectures require predictable interconnects to preserve precise event timing. Statically scheduled time-division-multiplexed (TDM) circuit-switched networks-on-chip (NoCs) provide deterministic latency at the cost of linear configuration-memory scaling with schedule depth. Furthermore, jointly optimizing task placement, routing, and scheduling creates an intractable combinatorial search space. Existing deployment frameworks also ignore algorithmic axonal delays by forcing immediate spike injections that increase network contention. This paper proposes a hardware-software co-design to address these challenges. ChroNoC is a tableless TDM NoC that embeds precomputed full-grid broadcast trees into combinational logic as a fixed routing substrate. items.title: Nonreciprocal magneto-optic beam steering of thermal emission
items.abstract: Conventional thermal emitters obey Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation, which ties absorptivity to emissivity and places a fundamental limit on a range of radiative energy technologies and sensing systems. This constraint can be overcome using magneto-optic materials, which exhibit nonreciprocal thermal emission under an applied magnetic field. While the spectral nonreciprocity of magneto-optic devices has been explored theoretically and experimentally, nonreciprocal control over the direction of thermal emission has received far less attention. Here, we propose and numerically demonstrate nonreciprocal beam steering of thermal emission, wherein an applied magnetic field lifts the degeneracy between guided modes at +/- kx, enabling asymmetric and tunable directional thermal emission. items.title: Emergent parafermions with tunable localization in a quantum circuit network
items.abstract: \noindent Quantum circuit simulators with hybrid metal-semiconductor dots provide a versatile platform to realize Kondo anyons. These arise at critical points driven by frustrated Kondo screening of dot charge degrees of freedom and have been demonstrated experimentally in linear circuits of one or two dots. Here we study a triangular triple dot device, where geometric frustration gives rise to an emergent $\mathbb{Z}_3$ parafermion shared among the three dots. We show that the parafermion can be tunably relocated to any pair of dots by applying gate voltages, and is supported in both the weak-tunneling `Kondo limit' and the strong transmission `quasiballistic' regime. The critical states survive strong coupling to external leads and other dots, establishing the basis for a scalable and reconfigurable network architecture in which non-Abelian excitations can be realized and manipulated.

items.title: When Protection Hurts: A Cytokine Storm Theory of Supply Chain Overreaction
items.abstract: Supply chain resilience research has traditionally viewed defensive actions such as safety stock, backup suppliers, expedited transportation, and emergency sourcing as beneficial. However, disruptions such as the COVID-19 pandemic, the 2021 semiconductor shortage, and the Suez Canal blockage highlight how synchronized hoarding, duplicate ordering, and capacity reservation can amplify congestion and operational costs, sometimes worsening the original disruption. Motivated by this observation, we develop a decision-theoretic framework in which Protective Response Intensity (PRI) is an endogenous decision variable. We introduce Response-Induced Loss (RIL) to capture costs generated by defensive actions and characterize a unique optimal response that balances disruption mitigation against self-induced losses. items.title: A Rowhammer attack on Fil-C's software capabilities
items.abstract: Rowhammer is a hardware vulnerability in dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) in which repeated accesses to one or more aggressor rows can induce bit-flips in nearby victim rows. This phenomenon violates a core assumption of conventional programming language semantics: that reading from or writing to one memory location does not modify others. Despite the security importance of this phenomenon, there is no widely established formal framework connecting Rowhammer faults with program behaviour. This makes it difficult to reason rigorously about the efficacy of proposed Rowhammer defences and the program-level guarantees they provide. To address this gap, we present a probabilistic small-step operational semantics for an idealised imperative language subject to Rowhammer-style faults. The semantics is high-level in that it abstracts from DRAM internals and semiconductor physics. A general pr...

items.title: Optical imaging with only the evanescent fields and without diffraction
items.abstract: We report on a conceptual framework for optical imaging utilizing exclusively evanescent fields, effectively eliminating or attenuating standard optical diffraction. We present the theoretical foundation of this concept based on the decomposition of dipole radiation into evanescent fields and homogeneous propagating waves, exploring the explicit conditions required to suppress the latter. By successfully decoupling and removing the homogeneous component, optical tasks, such as sub-diffraction imaging, can be executed solely via evanescent channels, bypassing traditional diffractive limits. We discuss the physical feasibility of this approach and provide concrete examples of how this conjecture can be realized using currently available laboratory and industrial techniques. The realization of this concept promises to redefine core paradigms in optics and fundamental physics. Because the mi...

items.title: Charge state and hydration of vacancies in silicon and silicon carbide in contact with water: A grand-canonical first-principles stability map
items.abstract: The state of a vacancy in a semiconductor is normally described by the Fermi level alone. In wet-etched, electrochemically processed, or humid silicon and silicon carbide, a vacancy also takes up hydrogen and oxygen from water, in amounts set by pH and electrode potential. We treat both effects together by minimizing the grand potential of a vacancy complex over its charge state and hydrogen/oxygen content. The result is a stability map in Fermi level and hydrogen chemical potential, which the computational hydrogen electrode relates to pH and potential. We parameterize it with spin-polarized density functional theory in 64-atom cells, including the vibrational free energy of bound H and O, for the silicon vacancy, its H, O, and OH complexes, and both vacancies of 3C-SiC. items.title: Physics Informed Neural Networks for Solving the Drift-Diffusion Equations
items.abstract: The drift-diffusion equations are the fundamental building block for the modeling, design, and optimization of modern semiconductor devices. Solutions of the drift-diffusion equations rarely give way to analytical forms, and exhibit strong nonlinearity, with the solutions ranging over several orders of magnitude. These attributes have led to research into numerical solvers, and while many commercial Technology Computer Aided Design (TCAD) packages now exist, they may require long simulation times, exhibit sensitivity to initial guesses, and rely on mesh generation. Further, these solvers are not well suited for inverse problems where the design parameters of a device are retrieved from its desired functional characteristics. To address all these challenges, this work demonstrates the usage of Physics Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for the solution of the drift-diffusion equations with...

items.title: Automated Multi-Line Bug Repair Using Model Checker Aided LLMs: A Case Study on RISC-V Processors
items.abstract: Functional verification of Register-Transfer Level(RTL) designs has become a critical bottleneck in modern semiconductor development, often consuming the majority of project resources. Debugging, in particular, remains an especially time-consuming task, requiring careful analysis of simulation traces or counterexamples. Recent work has explored applying Large Language Models (LLMs) to RTL debug and repair with great promise. However, the existing approaches typically are for single-line bugs, operate in open-loop, rely heavily on prompts or retrieval, lack scalability, and often produce incorrect fixes. In this paper, we propose a novel automated RTL bug repair methodology that combines LLMs, assertions, and a model checker to provide scalable, trustworthy semantic grounding and formal guarantees. items.title: Intrinsic Raman Modes and Crystal Symmetry of Altermagnetic $α$-MnTe
items.abstract: Crystal symmetry governs the physical properties of materials and provides the framework for interpreting their microscopic excitations and macroscopic responses. In altermagnets, the crystal symmetries that relate opposite-spin sublattices give rise to momentum-dependent spin splitting despite compensated magnetization. Determining the real crystal symmetry is therefore essential for understanding the intrinsic electronic and magnetic properties. For the altermagnetic semiconductor $α$-MnTe, conflicting Raman assignments have left both its intrinsic lattice excitations and its crystal symmetry unresolved. items.abstract: Monoclinic $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ is a promising ultra-wide-bandgap semiconductor for power electronics, but its low and anisotropic thermal conductivity limits heat removal, making it a compelling model system for nanoscale thermal transport studies. Here, we demonstrate a pronounced nanoscale enhancement of thermal anisotropy and uncover the underlying phonon mechanism by combining complementary thermal and acoustic spectroscopy techniques with first-principles calculations. Anisotropic thermoreflectance thermometry determines the full thermal-conductivity tensor from angular measurements within the (100), (010), and (001) crystallographic planes. Angle-resolved Brillouin light scattering reveals that low-frequency acoustic phonons exhibit only weak velocity anisotropy, insufficient to account for the measured thermal anisotropy. items.title: Structural characterization of the rutile-GeO2/TiO2 (001) heterointerface
items.abstract: Rutile-GeO2 (r-GeO2) has emerged as a promising ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) semiconductor for future high-power device applications because of its favorable combination of physical and electrical properties. This study has used high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) to compare heterointerfaces between thin films of GeO2 grown by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition on closely-lattice-matched rutile TiO2 (r-TiO2) substrates at temperatures of 840° C and 925° C. Cross-sectional TEM observations reveal interfaces with two entirely different structures: an amorphous GeOx/r-TiO2 heterostructure with an abrupt, highly faceted and non-planar interface, or a fully epitaxial r-GeO2/r-TiO2 heterostructure characterized by a more wavy but often facetted interface. items.title: Optical signatures of Rashba--Dresselhaus coupling across Franz--Keldysh and Landau regimes in two-dimensional semiconductors
items.abstract: We develop a unified theory of the interband optical response of a two-dimensional semiconductor with simultaneous Rashba and Dresselhaus spin-orbit couplings in electric and magnetic fields. In crossed fields, the in-plane electric field generates an effective spin-orbit drift field that modifies the Landau spectrum and spinor states, while at zero magnetic field the problem maps onto Landau--Zener spin dynamics.At zero external fields, the total joint density of states above the band gap remains unchanged, while characteristic subgap structures appear. Pure Rashba coupling produces an inverse square root singularity, whereas a finite Dresselhaus term gives a step and a logarithmic peak, allowing the two couplings to be distinguished optically. At zero magnetic field, the Franz--Keldysh response shows a crossover from diabatic to adiabatic spin dynamics as the electric field is reduced....

Although these models demonstrated remarkable speedup in circuit simulations, they were not rigorously tested in complex tasks within standard EDA tool flows for chip design, which require very high transistor model precision to provide accurate results and converge properly. To investigate their full potential and promise, we develop NN-based transistor models that accurately predict the drain current and various charges for a 3nm nanosheet, and employ the models for a standard cell library characterization. items.title: The Reaction of Financial Markets to the Releases of DeepSeek R1 and Kimi K3: A Critical Analysis
items.abstract: This paper compares financial-market reactions to the releases of DeepSeek R1 in January 2025 and Kimi K3 in July 2026. Both AI models were presented as credible Chinese competitors near the capability frontier, but their releases conveyed different economic information. DeepSeek R1 combined open weights with unusually low reported training and inference costs, prompting investors to reassess expected demand for computing infrastructure and producing large stock-price decreases among semiconductor and data-centre-related firms. Kimi K3 instead entered at broadly frontier prices and generated a market reaction concentrated more heavily among rival Chinese AI laboratories. items.title: Localization Contrast As a Fundamental Limit of Radiative Quantum Efficiency
items.abstract: Disorder can localize valence- and conduction-band states to different degrees, yet whether such localization contrast has observable consequences remains poorly understood. Here, we show that localization contrast strongly impacts competing carrier-recombination channels. We illustrate this behavior in random In$_x$Ga$_{1-x}$N alloys. Increasing the In content from $x=13.5\%$ to $x=22\%$ progressively localizes the valence-band maximum state while leaving the conduction-band minimum state comparatively delocalized. This contrasting localization decreases the interband optical momentum matrix element underlying radiative recombination. For Auger-Meitner recombination, however, localization alone does not determine the coupling; atomic-scale disorder also breaks primitive-cell translational symmetry and modifies the momentum-space and phase structure of the states. This generates addition...

items.title: Strain-induced structural transformations in hexagonal monolayer boron nitride. A density functional study
items.abstract: In this work we theoretically study the structural transformations occurring in monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) subjected to strong deformations. The first-principle computer simulations are based on the density functional theory employing the pseudopotentials with the exchange-correlation energy given in Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof form. Depending on the direction and the type of the strain, the simulations reveal different types of structural transformations in two-dimensional (2D) h-BN associated with the elastic failure. It is found that, under certain shear strains, there can form an ordered 2D orthorhombic phase with the 2D layer space symmetry pmmm. Thermal stability of the latter up to ~900 K is demonstrated by first-principle Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics. items.title: Electrically Pumped Quadratic-Soliton Mode-Locked Laser in Lithium Niobate Nanophotonics
items.abstract: Femtosecond mode-locked lasers are the workhorse of modern photonics, enabling optical atomic clocks, frequency combs, precision spectroscopy, and ultrafast signal processing. Bringing them onto nanophotonic chips promises miniaturized ultrafast systems, yet combining femtosecond pulse generation with electrical pumping remains a major challenge, rooted in a trade-off between the speed and energy efficiency of mode-locking mechanisms. Kerr-based mechanisms offer nearly instantaneous response but typically require high intracavity peak powers that are difficult to achieve with nanophotonic-compatible semiconductor gain. Conversely, semiconductor saturable absorbers enable strong nonlinear responses at low energies but are limited by their slow carrier dynamics. items.title: Electronic, structural and magnetic properties of goldene nanoribbons
items.abstract: Recently, two-dimensional goldene, a single-atomic-layer gold sheet, has been experimentally realized and is expected to be a promising material for next-generation devices, offering new possibilities beyond three-dimensional bulk gold. Because quasi-one-dimensional derivatives can exhibit properties markedly different from their two-dimensional counterparts, we investigate the stability, electronic, and magnetic properties of goldene-based nanoribbons (GOLDNRs) using first-principles computational methods. Our findings demonstrate that the electronic structure of these nanoribbons depends strongly on both edge chirality and ribbon width. Depending on the boundary configuration, the systems can exhibit semiconducting behavior with electronic band gaps of approximately 0.77 eV and 0.04 eV, or retain metallic characteristics. items.title: HAWK: Heterogeneity-Aware KV Cache Transfer for Efficient GPU-NPU Phase-Disaggregated LLM Inference
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference exhibits distinct computational characteristics across its two phases: prefill is compute-intensive, whereas decode is more memory-bound. As a result, AI accelerators achieve varying levels of efficiency across the two phases. GPUs are well suited to prefill, but are often underutilized during decode. By contrast, NPUs can utilize their compute resources more effectively during decode. Motivated by this observation, we explore a heterogeneous architecture that integrates GPUs and NPUs, mapping prefill to GPUs and decode to NPUs to achieve high performance and efficiency. However, realizing such heterogeneous integration is challenging because LLM phase disaggregation requires KV cache transfer from prefill to decode (that is, from GPUs to NPUs), which is complicated by differences in inter-device communication mechanisms and KV cache tensor layouts. items.title: Framework to identify defect-insensitive electron transport in topological semimetals
items.abstract: Topological semimetals are of increasing interest to replace conventional metals for interconnects in future semiconductor chips, due to their potential to exhibit decreasing resistivity with reducing wire dimensions and a lower sensitivity to electron scattering at defects. First-principles evaluation of promising topological semimetals for interconnects typically employ non-equilibrium Green's functions (NEGF) techniques to estimate defect scattering, but such calculations for specific defect geometries are difficult to systematize and compare between disparate materials. Here, we develop an NEGF-based approach to systematically and rapidly evaluate the defect sensitivity of electron transport in materials without depending on material-specific defect geometries. items.title: Observation of Size-dependent Optical Modes and Confinement in Fin Cavities using Angle-Resolved Cathodoluminescence
items.abstract: We observe novel optical fringes and emission coherence in laterally formed semiconductor fins using wavelength- and angle-resolved cathodoluminescence (WARCL). These findings demonstrate that cavity mode and emission confinement are directly governed by cavity geometry including cavity dimensions, facet angles, and orientation. In flat fins narrowing the width from 3000 nm to 200 nm sharpens fringe intensity, indicating stronger mode confinement and increased coherence. Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations confirm that the observed fringes originate from internal reflections among the fin facets, consistent with a Fabry-Pérot (FP) cavity model where the cavity length determines the fringe spacing. items.title: Large anisotropic magnetoresistance in paramagnetic Fe-doped Ta4SiTe4
items.abstract: Large anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) usually relies on magnetic ordering, which fixes a preferred moment orientation and couples it to charge transport. Here, we demonstrate that pronounced AMR can instead arise from the anisotropic magnetic-field-induced polarization of dilute local moments in paramagnetic Fe-doped Ta4SiTe4, a quasi-one-dimensional van der Waals narrow-gap semiconductor. Magnetization measurements reveal Curie-like paramagnetism down to 2 K, with the c axis as the magnetic easy axis. The magnetization is described by an effective S = 1/2 model with an anisotropic g-factor ratio of g_c/g_ab = 1.43(1). With the electrical current applied along the c axis, the Fe-doped sample exhibits a large negative magnetoresistance for B//c and only a weak positive response for B//ab, whereas the undoped sample shows little magnetoresistance for either field orientation. items.title: Coherent dynamics and ultrafast evolution of optical nonlinearity of self-hybridized exciton-polaritons in WSe2
items.abstract: Exciton-polaritons (EPs) are valuable for investigating macroscopic quantum coherent phenomena. However, overcoming the rapid decoherence of EPs under ambient conditions is challenging, even using delicately fabricated optical cavities. Here, we show pronounced coherent dynamics in thin flakes of WSe2 supporting self-hybridized EPs. Ultrafast two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy (2DES) resolves two types of quantum beating: Rabi oscillation with a period of ~ 24 fs and a slower, ~ 50 fs period oscillation, revealing coherent coupling not only between excitons and cavity, but also between polaritons and dark states. Rapid evolution of 2DES line shape indicates a change of dominant optical nonlinearities from Rabi contraction of polaritons to many-body interactions of excitons in the first 100 fs, marking the transition from coherent to incoherent polariton excitations. items.title: The Spectroscopic Atlas of Excitonic Complexes in hBN-Encapsulated S-TMD Monolayers: From Excitons to Oxcitons and Beyond
items.abstract: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) encapsulation has transformed the optical spectroscopy of semiconducting transition-metal dichalcogenide monolayers (MLs) by suppressing extrinsic disorder and enabling the resolution of an increasingly complex hierarchy of excitonic states. This Review provides a spectroscopy-oriented framework for understanding and identifying excitonic complexes in hBN-encapsulated Mo- and W-based MLs and their alloys. The discussion covers bright and dark excitons, Rydberg states, charged excitons, biexcitons, phonon-assisted replicas, and higher-order Fermi-sea many-body states, including hexcitons and oxcitons, with an emphasis on the experimental signatures that distinguish them. items.title: Online Open-World Wafer Defect Discovery using Hyperdimensional Computing
items.abstract: Conventional wafer defect analysis relies on offline, closed-world classifiers that fail to detect novel, unseen defect signatures emerging during continuous semiconductor manufacturing. To address this, we propose WaferHDC, an online open-world wafer defect discovery framework based on hyperdimensional computing (HDC). The memory-centric architecture of WaferHDC enables rapid anomaly detection and grouping of recurring failures into compact hypervector representations. This allows the memory space to dynamically scale with new defect modes without retraining a static classifier or archiving entire raw wafer history. WaferHDC first models normal spatial distributions, then dynamically groups recurring failures into persistent defect memory without labels or predefined class counts. It outperforms the strongest online baseline by 13.3 p.p. in adjusted Rand index and 10.5 p.p. in normalize...

items.title: Ultrafast and Anisotropic Exciton Transport in Layered NbOI$_2$
items.abstract: Ferroelectric layered semiconductors provide a unique platform for exploring coupled excitonic and electronic phenomena in reduced dimensions. Here, exciton transport in layered NbOI$_2$ is investigated using transient absorption microscopy. Ultrafast and strongly anisotropic exciton diffusion is observed. The diffusion coefficient of about 160 cm$^2$ s$^{-1}$ along the nonpolar crystal axis is among the highest reported for van der Waals semiconductors. The transport exhibits an approximately twofold in-plane anisotropy between the polar and nonpolar directions, reflecting the intrinsic low-symmetry crystal structure of NbOI$_2$. The environmental stability of NbOI$_2$ is further investigated, and fabrication and encapsulation conditions required to achieve long-term sample stability are identified. These results establish NbOI$_2$ as a promising platform for studying anisotropic excito...

items.title: Accelerating real-time hybrid-functional calculations with learned ACE and symmetry-based FFT reuse
items.abstract: Real-time hybrid-functional calculations require repeated reconstruction of nonlocal exchange, whose cost grows rapidly with Brillouin-zone sampling. We develop two methods to improve the efficiency of time evolution and spatial processing. The first learns the time evolution of adaptively compressed exchange (ACE) factors and predicts their updates, reducing the frequency of explicit reconstruction. The second uses crystal symmetry to reuse exchange fast Fourier transforms (FFTs) among equivalent real-space points. This symmetry-based FFT reuse (SBFR) reduces the number of FFTs while retaining the full $\bm k$-point sum. The methods can be used with a variety of hybrid functionals, and we use HSE06 in this work. Relative to an ACE reference using full-row mesh FFTs, learned prediction provides more than fivefold acceleration, SBFR more than fourteenfold, and their combination more than...

items.title: Nanophotonic Extreme Ultraviolet Polarimeter
items.abstract: Nanophotonic engineering has revolutionized how we manipulate the polarization of visible light. Here, we extend such control to extreme ultraviolet radiation, the spectral region of attosecond science and semiconductor lithography, where transmissive optical elements are lacking. We implement channel waveguides that restrict incident 41-nm-wavelength light to a few modes with defined spatial profiles and propagation constants. By designing the propagation-length-dependent interference of two eigenmodes, we achieve polarization-dependent forward scattering, which we exploit to create a transmissive nanophotonic analyzer that resolves the polarization axis and spectrum of extreme ultraviolet light from a single measurement. With a 0.9°-sensitivity for polarization rotations in a 1-second measurement and single-shot capability, the device opens new experimental opportunities in ultrafast m...

items.title: Charge-conserving creation and annihilation of topological phase singularities in atomically thin semiconductors
items.abstract: Atomically thin transition metal dichalcogenides provide a promising material platform for optical phase manipulation, as rapid variations in their dielectric functions can give rise to topological phase singularities (PSs). However, PS evolution while preserving topological charge conservation has not yet been investigated in exciton enabled PS systems. Here, using atomically thin MoS2 films on sapphire as a model system, we theoretically and experimentally demonstrate that the evolution of dielectric dispersion determines the creation, trajectory, merging, and annihilation of optical PSs under topological charge conservation. By varying the MoS2 film thickness, we experimentally realize this evolution through the gradual shrinking of the high energy n-k dispersion loop, which modifies its intersection with the zero reflection condition. Our results provide a general strategy for explor...

items.title: Nanocrystalline cubic boron arsenide growth on GaAs(100) by gas source molecular beam epitaxy
items.abstract: Cubic boron arsenide (c-BAs) is a promising ultrahigh thermal conductivity semiconductor, but its direct synthesis on lattice-mismatched substrates remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the synthesis of nanocrystalline c-BAs thin films on GaAs(100) substrates using gas source molecular beam epitaxy. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals an optimal growth temperature window of 250-400 C to maintain near stoichiometry and suppress severe arsenic loss. Surface and structural characterizations via atomic force microscopy, reflection high-energy electron diffraction, and grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction demonstrate a Volmer-Weber 3D island growth mode and a preferential crystallographic alignment with the GaAs substrate. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy confirms a chemically sharp interface without gallium interdiffusion into the c-BAs layer. These findings establish...

items.title: Multi-Agent AI Design of a Nanowatt Biomedical Low-Pass Filter from Topology to Layout
items.abstract: We demonstrate a multi-agent framework that takes an analog circuit from topology synthesis to layout. A researcher agent directs schematic and layout agents, a four-tier memory stores the specification and lessons, and separate agents review the designs. Deterministic tools provide pass/fail simulation reports, symbolic analysis, graph-based netlist equivalence, parasitic injection, and extraction with DRC and LVS in every optimization trial. A human approves the specification and the layout plan. For a fourth-order, 250-Hz subthreshold biopotential low-pass filter, the researcher agent synthesized, through simulation-guided trial and error, a novel current-reuse architecture that shares a single dc bias branch between a super-source-follower biquad and a flipped-voltage-follower biquad. items.title: Two-qubit cryo-CMOS control of a spin register in diamond
items.abstract: Utility-scale quantum technologies will not only require a well-performing quantum platform, but also classical control hardware that is scalable, efficient, and meets the design requirements set by the quantum system of interest. One approach is the application of silicon CMOS technology, a highly scalable and mature technology, to design application-specific integrated circuits (ASIC) that are optimized for the quantum system. In this work, we present two-qubit control of electron and nuclear spins in NV centres in diamond, using a cryogenic CMOS qubit controller integrated with a diamond quantum device in a cryostat. Using Gate Set Tomography (GST) we characterize the performance of the single-qubit gates on both electron- and carbon nuclear spins, and analyze the limiting noise processes. items.abstract: High-Dynamic-Range (HDR) multi-band linear polarimetry of the solar corona during total solar eclipses provides a vital ground-based diagnostic tool for mapping plasma morphology and magnetic topology in the inner and middle corona. Extracting reliable polarimetric signals requires rigorous observational calibration, spatial co-alignment, and noise reduction via stacking. We report optical linear polarimetric observations acquired during the 8 April 2024 total solar eclipse from Dallas, Texas, USA, near solar maximum. items.title: Privacy-Preserving Robust Monitoring of Dense-Time Temporal Logic
items.abstract: Motivated by the use of third-party testing, this paper presents a privacy-preserving implementation of the robustness monitoring of Signal Temporal Logic (STL). STL is a specification language for systems whose output traces have real-valued timestamps -- most prominently, cyber-physical systems. Its robust semantics, which assign real rather than binary truth values, are an essential ingredient of systems testing and runtime monitoring. In a number of system testing scenarios, the designer and the tester are separate parties. This testing-as-a-service model is common in software, avionics, and semiconductors, and is growing in importance in the red-teaming of machine learning models. In such a model, the designer seeks to preserve the privacy (or secrecy) of its design, while the tester seeks to preserve the privacy of its collateral, including the detailed specification suite. This pa...

items.title: Anchored Exploration in Product Evolution: A Phylogenetic Network Framework for Semiconductor Designs
items.abstract: We develop a product phylogenetic network framework for examining anchored exploration. Using 102,465 semiconductor products grouped into 45,996 design families, we distinguish accumulated design continuity (Anchor) from externally precedented feature additions (horizontal transfer, HT). Fitted regressions yield non-monotonic relationships for HT occurrence and descendant carriage, alongside increasing within-family carriage over observed support. These patterns connect technological trajectories and recombination by distinguishing the continuity associated with incorporating external features from that associated with reproducing them in subsequent products.

items.title: Superradiant temporal transition radiation of a relativistic electron beam
items.abstract: A charge in uniform motion carries a bound field that does not radiate. Transition radiation releases part of it at a boundary in space. We propose and analyze the case of radiation emission due to a boundary in time: a relativistic electron bunch passes through an aperture in a semiconductor (silicon) wafer, and while its bound field occupies the wafer, a femtosecond laser switches the semiconductor into an electron-hole plasma. The field is a valid solution of the old medium and not of the new one, so it is handed to the plasma as an initial condition for radiation emission at the plasma frequency. Because in temporal transition radiation (t-TR) the wavevector is conserved, and the frequency is not, the emission can appear in a spectral band that the bunch's own field does not populate. Every electron contributes in phase to the initial condition at the switching moment, so the emitted...

items.title: Molecular Doping of MoS$_2$ with N-Heterocyclic Carbenes: A Raman Study of Interfacial Charge Transfer
items.abstract: We demonstrate efficient electron doping of exfoliated MoS$_2$ through the deposition of N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) molecules onto its surface. Raman spectroscopy reveals a pronounced softening of the optical A$_{1g}$ phonon mode after NHC deposition, consistent with electron transfer from the NHC molecules to the MoS$_2$ layers. The largest phonon-energy shifts are observed in monolayer and bilayer flakes whereas changes in bulk-like MoS$_2$ are negligible, indicating that the doping efficiency depends on the number of layers. This thickness dependence highlights the dominant role of interfacial charge transfer at the NHC/MoS$_2$ interface. items.title: Concatenated continuous-drive protection of exchange-based spin-qubit gates
items.abstract: Exchange-based two-qubit gates in semiconductor spin qubits are sensitive to low-frequency detuning noise and control errors. Here, we extend concatenated continuous driving (CCD), implemented by phase modulation of a global microwave drive, to exchange-based SWAP and $\sqrt{\mathrm{SWAP}}$ operations between double-dressed spin qubits and investigate its effectiveness for protecting two-qubit gates. We find that CCD retains strong protection against quasistatic common-mode detuning errors while substantially improving robustness against Rabi-frequency errors and qubit-to-qubit Rabi-frequency mismatch compared with conventional continuous dressing. By contrast, the gate fidelity is impacted by differential detuning errors. items.title: Water-Driven Porous Silicon as a Platform for Blue Materials
items.abstract: Living organisms control water to transport matter, transfer energy and drive chemical reactions. In this perspective, we argue that porous silicon can give engineering materials comparable control over water. Its pore architecture, surface chemistry and semiconducting skeleton can be shaped across length scales with the precision of semiconductor processing and, like the water it can host, it relies on one of the most abundant chemical elements on Earth. Liquids in porous silicon, most often water, can flow as a continuum through pores a few nanometers wide, strain the skeleton through capillary and electrosorption stresses, shift structural color, switch transparency, and modulate or generate electrical signals. items.abstract: Moiré semiconductors provide a physical realization of the Hubbard model. items.title: Theoretical study of nitrogen-vacancy spin coherence enhanced by vacancy aggregation in diamond using cluster-correlation expansion
items.abstract: Annealing a semiconductor makes its vacancies mobile; they aggregate into multi-vacancy complexes that often carry spin. Such centres are a magnetic-noise source for any spin qubit among them, in silicon and silicon carbide as well as in diamond, and they are accordingly blamed for NV- decoherence in irradiated and implanted diamond, with two coherence records credited to removing them. Cluster-correlation-expansion simulations driven by published electron-paramagnetic-resonance parameters invert that attribution. At a fixed paramagnetic spin density a multi-vacancy bath gives a Hahn-echo coherence time 3.1-7.1 times longer than a bath of isolated negative vacancies, over three decades of concentration. A bath dephases the qubit because its spins exchange spin projections with one another, and two can exchange only if their transition frequencies match. A fine-structure splitting shifts...

items.title: SimSkip: StrongARM-Comparator Similarity Sensing with SAR-Skipping-Aware Training for Analog Compute-in-Memory
items.abstract: Analog-to-digital conversion dominates the energy and area of analog compute-in-memory (CIM) accelerators. This paper presents SimSkip, a successive-approximation-register (SAR) skipping scheme that combines a lightweight StrongARM-comparator similarity detector with SAR-skipping-aware training. When two held voltages are similar, the upper bits of the preceding code are reused to skip SAR comparisons. Detector-induced disturbance extracted from 55-nm CMOS simulations and bit-exact prefix saturation are embedded in the forward pass, and the network learns to tolerate them through quantization-aware training and knowledge distillation. On an ISAAC-based W4A4 WRN-28-10, SimSkip achieves 77.23% CIFAR-100 top-1 accuracy (mean of three seeds) versus 78.4% for the baseline, while reducing SAR comparisons by 48.2% across three hardware-modeled layers. A first-order model estimates a 27.2% net A...

items.title: A semiconductor photon-pair source based on a polariton cascade
items.abstract: We present a theoretical study of a semiconductor photon-pair source based on a radiative cascade enabled by a permanent exciton dipole. The source consists of a GaAs quantum dot placed between a metal nanoparticle and a mirror. The dot exciton and the localized electromagnetic mode mix to form upper and lower polaritons. Without a permanent dipole, a symmetry separating states with even and odd excitation numbers forbids photon emission between the polaritons. Separation of the mean electron and hole positions gives the exciton a permanent dipole and breaks this symmetry. The upper polariton can then emit an idler photon as it decays to the lower polariton. The lower polariton can emit a signal photon as the system returns to its ground state. Using an effective model, we calculate the probability that a prepared upper polariton emits both photons through the metal antenna. We also anal...

items.title: Accelerating Periodic Coupled Cluster and Algebraic Diagrammatic Construction Theories With Frozen Natural Orbitals
items.abstract: We present a unified frozen natural orbital (FNO) framework for periodic Gaussian-orbital post-Hartree-Fock calculations with explicit k-point sampling. The approach includes conventional ground-state FNOs together with state-specific (SS-FNO) and state-averaged (SA-FNO) variants constructed from perturbative one-particle density matrices. We implement these approximations for periodic Moller-Plesset perturbation theory, algebraic diagrammatic construction, and equation-of-motion coupled cluster methods in the PySCF software package and benchmark them for correlation energies, equations of state, fundamental band gaps, and quasiparticle band structures of semiconductors and insulators. FNO truncation reproduces canonical results with small errors while substantially reducing computational cost. SS-FNO enables accurate large-basis band-gap calculations, including quadruple-zeta results, w...

items.title: JANUS: A Multi-modal Foundation Neural Sampler for Disordered Materials
items.abstract: Disordered materials are central to modern technologies, from high-performance alloys to quantum devices, yet understanding and designing them requires exploring an enormous space of compositions and atomic arrangements. Here we introduce JANUS, a multimodal neural sampler that jointly explores chemical composition, atomic structure and volume, learning directly from the energy of the system without requiring pre-generated equilibrium configurations. Across test systems, JANUS reproduces reference equilibrium properties and recovers free energy and phase behavior with about three orders of magnitude fewer energy evaluations than reference Monte Carlo sampling. In multicomponent alloys, JANUS reproduces experimentally observed local chemical order and can be steered to further enhance chemical order and stiffness. Coupled to an evolutionary language model agent, it also enables efficient...

items.title: Inverse-Designed High-Q and Small-Mode-Volume Silicon Nitride Photonic Crystal Cavities for Second- and Third-Harmonic Generation
items.abstract: SiN photonic crystal (PhC) cavities are promising platforms for nonlinear and quantum photonics because of their wide transparency window, CMOS compatibility, and negligible two-photon absorption. However, realizing high-Q/V cavities remains challenging because of the relatively low refractive index of SiN. Here, we employ inverse design to optimize a two-dimensional SiN PhC cavity and experimentally demonstrate a quality factor of approximately 80,000, the highest reported for a near-stoichiometric SiN 2D PhC cavity. Furthermore, both second- and third-harmonic generation are observed from the same cavity, providing experimental evidence of strong optical confinement and large Q/V. Our results establish inverse-designed SiN PhC cavities as a promising platform for nonlinear photonics and future heterogeneous integrated photonic devices.

items.title: Real-Time FPGA-Based Multi-Parameter Feedback Stabilization of a Silicon Double Quantum Dot
items.abstract: Long term operation of semiconductor spin qubits requires active stabilization of quantum dot potentials against low-frequency charge noise. To address this, we demonstrate a gradient-descent feedback approach in a silicon double quantum dot device using high-bandwidth radio-frequency (rf) reflectometry readout and a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) for digital signal processing. This architecture enables continuous multi-parameter gradient calculation and quick gate voltage updates, significantly increasing the effective feedback bandwidth compared to previous methods relying on slow direct-current transport measurements. By operating with 8 steps per feedback cycle and an integration time of 25.6 $μ$s, this high-speed stabilization scheme maintains better than -6 dB of noise suppression up to 5 kHz, achieving an attenuation of $-7.4 \pm 0.2$ dB at the maximum measured frequency. items.title: Odd-even dichotomy in the waveforms of modified Emden oscillators of arbitrary integer power
items.abstract: Closed-form waveforms of the modified Emden oscillators $\ddot x+(q+2)kx^q\dot x+k^2x^{2q+1}+ω^2x=0$ of arbitrary natural power $q$, and of their damped $c$-deformed versions, are obtained through a generalized commutative factorization that reduces them to Bernoulli equations. We show that commutative factorizations of Liénard equations are gauge-conjugated forms of the nonlocal linearizing transformation of Chandrasekar, Senthilvelan, Kundu and Lakshmanan, the factorization constant being half the difference of the roots of the associated linear oscillator. These oscillators display an odd--even dichotomy: for odd $q$ they are isochronous, with period $2π/ω$ independent of the amplitude, within an explicitly bounded range of the integration constant, while for even $q$ the oscillations decay algebraically, as $t^{-1/q}$. items.title: Strain engineering of transient exciton diffusion in WSe2 monolayers at cryogenic temperatures
items.abstract: Tungsten-based transition metal dichalcogenides exhibit dark excitons as the energetically lowest states. These are crucial for exciton thermalization and propagation and they dominate low-temperature photoluminescence via the emergence of pronounced phonon sidebands. After a resonant excitation, highly mobile hot dark excitons are formed, which quickly thermalize into an equilibrium distribution. The application of strain modifies the exciton energy landscape and, in particular, the relative energy separation between bright and dark exciton states. The impact of strain on the transient photoluminescence and diffusion of non-equilibrium excitons has remained largely unexplored so far. In this work, we investigate the spatiotemporal exciton dynamics in strained hBN-encapsulated WSe2 monolayers at cryogenic temperatures. We demonstrate that tensile strain abruptly increases the excess ener...

items.title: THz-Driven Floquet Spin Valve-Modulator
items.abstract: Within the scattering matrix ($S$-matrix) framework adapted to the high-frequency Floquet--Magnus formalism based on the length gauge, we investigate spin-dependent quantum transport in a 1D quantum ring with an asymmetric ($π/2$) configuration of quantum point contacts. We demonstrate the realization of a contactless electromagnetic analog of the Datta--Das spin field-effect transistor with ferromagnetic leads operating at zero static magnetic field. It is shown that an off-resonance terahertz (THz) field enables high-precision switching between spin channels without altering the static parameters of the nanostructure. Driven by an electronic Vernier effect, the quantum interference in the asymmetric geometry yields a selective spin phase rotator alongside an ultra-high-contrast current-suppression regime (``optical shutter''). items.title: Decoherence of a quantum magneto-oscillator: Effect of field-bath interaction
items.abstract: We investigate the quantum dissipative dynamics of a charged magneto-oscillator(CMO) coupled to a heat bath of harmonic oscillators in the presence of an additional field-bath interaction. The problem is formulated within the framework of the generalized quantum Langevin equation, where the external confining potential modifies the random force correlations and the memory kernel of the environment, and the effective spring constant. Using the corresponding non-Markovian master equation, we examine the influence of the field-bath coupling on the temporal decay of the reduced density matrix of the system. We show that the additional interaction leads to an enhancement of the decoherence rate by altering the dissipative response of the bath. items.title: Parity-selected charging and noise-correlated work retention in a coupled Si/SiGe double quantum dot battery: theory and experimentally parameterized modeling
items.abstract: We investigate extractable work storage in a capacitively coupled double quantum dot (DQD) quantum battery (QB) subjected to experimentally motivated detuning charge noise. The battery is modeled as two interacting charge qubits with an Ising-type capacitive coupling and is charged by resonant microwave modulation of the tunnel coupling channel. Detuning fluctuations are introduced as classical stochastic processes generated from a band-limited 1/f noise spectrum. For each noise realization, the evolution remains unitary, whereas decoherence and loss of contrast emerge after ensemble averaging. We analyze the total ergotropy, its population and coherent contributions, the energy basis populations, a passive ordering violation diagnostic, and the Jensen-Shannon coherence of the noise-averaged state. items.title: High-Fidelity Synthetic Transmission Electron Microscopy Image Generation Using Diffusion Probabilistic Models for Data-Limited Semiconductor Metrology
items.abstract: Advanced semiconductor nodes drastically increased demand for Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), yet destructive sample preparation, slow imaging and high costs severely limit the availability of diverse datasets needed for downstream machine learning (ML). Synthetic data generation is becoming essential, but current generative models often miss TEM-specific noise, structural detail, and stochastic variability crucial for evaluation. We present a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) framework for synthetic TEM image generation under extreme data scarcity. A progressive patch-based training strategy scales from low-resolution patches to full images, enabling from-scratch training with only 15 samples. items.title: Quantum digital simulations of time-domain semiconductor spectroscopy in the semi-classical approximation
items.abstract: We present a digital quantum simulation framework for ultrafast optical spectroscopy of semiconductor materials. The framework is based on Brillouin-zone discretization and is designed as a quantum alternative to classical simulations based on the semiconductor Bloch equations. Its current capabilities include quantum simulations of linear absorption and optical gain, incorporating Lorentzian broadening, finite-temperature band-filling effects, and reduced-dimensionality effects. Comparison with classical simulations of GaAs within the single-particle approximation demonstrates quantitative agreement in the noiseless limit. The inclusion of realistic hardware noise characteristic of NISQ-era quantum computers effectively manifests as an additional source of scattering, resulting in increased spectral broadening. items.title: Electrically tunable Crossed Andreev Reflection in Bipolar Magnetic Semiconductors
items.abstract: Crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) is a nonlocal quantum transport phenomenon that arises at the interfaces between a superconductor and two spatially separated metals. In this process, an electron incident from one metal combines with another electron originating from the other metal to form a Cooper pair in the SC. In this work, we theoretically investigate the quantum transport properties of a device comprising a central $s$-wave superconductor sandwiched between two bipolar magnetic semiconductor (BMS) leads. BMS materials possess a unique bandstructure where the conduction and valence bands are fully spin-polarized in opposite directions. By applying independent gate voltages to the two BMS leads, we selectively tune their chemical potentials to configure an antiparallel spin alignment at the Fermi energy.
